title: Minimum Deletions to Make String Balanced
description:
# Minimum Deletions to Make String Balanced

Given a string `s` containing only `'a'` and `'b'`, delete the fewest characters so that the remaining string is **balanced**. A balanced string has no pair of indices `i < j` where `s[i] == 'b'` and `s[j] == 'a'`.

Equivalently, after deletions, the remaining string must have the form `aaa...bbb...`: zero or more `'a'` characters followed by zero or more `'b'` characters. Return the minimum number of deletions.

## Example 1:

**Input:** s = "aababbab"
**Output:** 2
**Explanation:** One optimal result is `aaabbb`, obtained by deleting one `'b'` and one later `'a'`.

## Example 2:

**Input:** s = "bbaaaaabb"
**Output:** 2
**Explanation:** Delete the first two `'b'` characters so all remaining `'a'` characters come before all remaining `'b'` characters.

## Constraints:

*   `1 <= s.length <= 10^5`
*   `s[i]` is either `'a'` or `'b'`.

tests.description: Alternating string requires deleting either early b's or later a's.
All b's before all a's forces deleting one whole side.
All a's before all b's remains unchanged.
Odd alternating pattern checks the split decision.
One late a after a b-run should cost one deletion.
A single trailing a after many b's is cheaper to delete than the b-run.
Large reversed blocks choose the smaller side.
Mixed middle blocks require comparing several cut positions.

solutions.name: One Pass DP Delete A Or Previous Bs
solutions.description:
## Approach

Scan from left to right. Keep `seenB`, the number of `'b'` characters already seen, and `deletions`, the minimum deletions needed to make the scanned prefix balanced. When the current character is `'b'`, it can stay at the end of the prefix. When it is `'a'` after previous `'b'` characters, choose the cheaper option: delete this `'a'`, or delete every previous unmatched `'b'`.

## Key Insight

The only new violation caused by reading an `'a'` is that it appears after earlier `'b'` characters. The optimal prefix answer is therefore updated by `min(delete this a, delete all previous b's)`.

## Complexity Analysis

The string is scanned once and only two counters are stored. Time Complexity: O(n). Space Complexity: O(1).
solutions.code: class Solution { public int minimumDeletions(String s) { int seenB = 0; int deletions = 0; for (char ch : s.toCharArray()) { if (ch == 'b') { seenB++; } else { deletions = Math.min(deletions + 1, seenB); } } return deletions; } }

solutions.name: Prefix Suffix Split Counts
solutions.description:
## Approach

Try every split position. Characters before the split should be kept as `'a'`, so every `'b'` on the left must be deleted. Characters after the split should be kept as `'b'`, so every `'a'` on the right must be deleted. Precompute prefix counts of left-side `'b'` characters and suffix counts of right-side `'a'` characters, then minimize their sum.

## Key Insight

Every balanced remaining string has a boundary between its kept `'a'` part and kept `'b'` part. Enumerating that boundary turns the problem into a cut-cost calculation.

## Complexity Analysis

Two auxiliary arrays store the left and right deletion costs for all cuts. Time Complexity: O(n). Space Complexity: O(n).
solutions.code: class Solution { public int minimumDeletions(String s) { int n = s.length(); int[] leftB = new int[n + 1]; int[] rightA = new int[n + 1]; for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) { leftB[i + 1] = leftB[i] + (s.charAt(i) == 'b' ? 1 : 0); } for (int i = n - 1; i >= 0; i--) { rightA[i] = rightA[i + 1] + (s.charAt(i) == 'a' ? 1 : 0); } int best = n; for (int cut = 0; cut <= n; cut++) { best = Math.min(best, leftB[cut] + rightA[cut]); } return best; } }

solutions.name: Greedy Stack Of Unmatched B
solutions.description:
## Approach

Think of kept `'b'` characters as a stack of unmatched blockers. When a `'b'` appears, add one blocker. When an `'a'` appears while blockers exist, delete one previous blocker instead of keeping a bad `b...a` inversion. Count how many blockers are removed.

## Key Insight

Deleting a previous unmatched `'b'` is equivalent to popping it from a stack. This greedy view makes the local repair concrete: every conflicting `'a'` either deletes itself or cancels one earlier `'b'`, and canceling the earlier blocker never makes a later conflict worse.

## Complexity Analysis

Only the count of unmatched blockers is needed; the actual stack contents are identical. Time Complexity: O(n). Space Complexity: O(1).
solutions.code: class Solution { public int minimumDeletions(String s) { int unmatchedB = 0; int deletions = 0; for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) { char ch = s.charAt(i); if (ch == 'b') { unmatchedB++; } else if (unmatchedB > 0) { unmatchedB--; deletions++; } } return deletions; } }

solutions.name: Longest Kept Balanced Subsequence
solutions.description:
## Approach

Instead of counting deletions directly, maximize how many characters can be kept. For a split position, the kept characters are all `'a'` characters before the split plus all `'b'` characters after it. Scan once while tracking `keptA` on the left, `remainingB` on the right, and the best kept length.

## Key Insight

Minimum deletions equals `n - maximum kept balanced subsequence length`. This is the same boundary idea as prefix/suffix counts, but expressed as a keep-maximization problem.

## Complexity Analysis

The algorithm counts total `'b'` values once and then scans the string once more. Time Complexity: O(n). Space Complexity: O(1).
solutions.code: class Solution { public int minimumDeletions(String s) { int totalB = 0; for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) { if (s.charAt(i) == 'b') { totalB++; } } int keptA = 0; int remainingB = totalB; int best = totalB; for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) { char ch = s.charAt(i); if (ch == 'a') { keptA++; } else { remainingB--; } best = Math.max(best, keptA + remainingB); } return s.length() - best; } }

solutions.name: Two-State Dynamic Programming
solutions.description:
## Approach

Maintain two DP states for the scanned prefix. `allA` is the minimum deletions needed to make the prefix contain only `'a'` characters. `balanced` is the minimum deletions needed to make the prefix balanced, allowing a final block of `'b'` characters. Update both states for each character.

## Key Insight

A balanced string has two phases: the all-`'a'` phase and the optional trailing-`'b'` phase. Once the DP has entered the trailing-`'b'` phase, a later `'a'` must be deleted unless we reinterpret the prefix as still being all `'a'`.

## Complexity Analysis

The two states are updated once per character. Time Complexity: O(n). Space Complexity: O(1).
solutions.code: class Solution { public int minimumDeletions(String s) { int allA = 0; int balanced = 0; for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) { char ch = s.charAt(i); int nextAllA = allA + (ch == 'b' ? 1 : 0); int nextBalanced; if (ch == 'a') { nextBalanced = Math.min(allA, balanced + 1); } else { nextBalanced = Math.min(allA, balanced); } allA = nextAllA; balanced = nextBalanced; } return balanced; } }
